families.product_name: LVivo Software Application (LVivo EF / LVivo Toolbox: EF, SG/SWM, Strain, SAX, RV, PLAX, CE-EF, Bladder)
families.company: DiA Imaging Analysis Ltd. (a Philips company since May 2023; earlier trade name DiACardio Ltd.)
deployment: on-device (Android option for LVivo EF; GE Vscan Extend app; Philips Lumify Auto EF)
ultrasound-system-embedded (Philips EPIQ CVx / Affiniti CVx per Philips 2024 release)
families.summary: Fully automated software that segments and tracks the left ventricular endocardium in DICOM echo clips to compute biplane (4CH/2CH) ejection fraction and volumes, with later modules adding segmental wall motion and longitudinal strain (2016), right-ventricular function via a deep-learning model and bladder volume (2020), a neural-network update to LVivo EF (2021), a parasternal long-axis module (2024), a contrast-enhanced EF module (2025), and a revised segmental wall-motion algorithm with an Age >18 indication (2025). First cleared in 2013 as LVivo EF (DiACardio) under product code LLZ; reclassified to QIH from 2020. DiA was acquired by Philips in May 2023; the LVivo EF algorithm is the basis of the Lumify Auto EF feature (K232500).
families.intended_use_quote: LVivo platform is intended for non-invasive processing of ultrasound images to detect, measure, and calculate relevant medical parameters of structures and function of patients with suspected disease.
families.indications_for_use_quote: LVivo platform is intended for non-invasive processing of ultrasound images to detect, measure, and calculate relevant medical parameters of structures and function of patients with suspected disease and Age >18. In addition, it has the ability to provide Quality Score feedback.
embedded_ai_features: Automated LV endocardial border detection and frame-by-frame tracking (image segmentation; neural network added to LVivo EF in K210053)
Automated ED/ES frame selection and biplane Simpson's EF/volumes
Global and segmental longitudinal strain (LVivo SG / LVivo Strain)
Segmental wall-motion scoring (machine-learning classifier; revised in K243862)
LVivo RV: deep-learning neural-network identification of RV endocardium and tricuspid annulus; EDA, ESA, FAC, TAPSE, S', free-wall strain
LVivo PLAX: automated LV size/function from parasternal long axis (fractional shortening)
LVivo CE-EF: EF from contrast-enhanced clips
LVivo Bladder: machine learning + active contour bladder segmentation and volume

clearances.changes_summary: Initial clearance of LVivo EF Software Application (DiACardio): fully automated biplane (4CH + 2CH) LV ejection fraction from DICOM echo clips.
Renamed LVivo Software Application; adds LVivoSG module for segmental wall-motion scoring, segmental longitudinal strain and global longitudinal strain (3 apical views); Linux support added.

New predicate TomTec-Arena (K132544); reference devices K161382, K130779, K180995. Product code moves to QIH. Adds LVivo RV (deep-learning neural network for RV endocardium and tricuspid annulus; ESA, EDA, FAC, TAPSE, S', free-wall strain), LVivo SAX, LVivo Bladder (non-cardiac), and an Android mobile option for LVivo EF. Indications broadened from LV-only to general ultrasound structures/function.
Special 510(k): LVivo EF algorithm modified by addition of a neural network; all other modules and indications unchanged.
notable_flags: neural network added to LVivo EF

clearances.changes_summary: Special 510(k) using LVivo IQS (K222970) as predicate. Adds LVivo PLAX module (automated LV size/function incl. fractional shortening from the parasternal long-axis view) with manual ED/ES frame selection for PLAX; IFU now includes Quality Score feedback. Module list: PLAX, IQS, EF, SG, SAX, RV, Seamless, Bladder.

Traditional 510(k); reference device Siemens ACUSON Sequoia (K232145). Adds LVivo CE-EF (Contrast EF) module for processing clips acquired with an ultrasound enhancing agent. OS listed as Windows 10 or higher.

Special 510(k): LVivo SWM (segmental wall motion) module modified ('Based on the same machine learning algorithm, multiple processing steps were added and the calculated features revised'); indications add 'Age >18'. Cybersecurity (SBOM, threat modelling) documented.

performance_claims.endpoint: Biplane LVEF agreement vs manual biplane (MBP)
performance_claims.dataset_description: Blinded clinical trial; 83 subjects (OCR of the 2013 summary is imperfect: 'r-0.88, p<OO0l')
performance_claims.quote: In the blinded clinical trial, ultrasound clips of 83 subjects were evaluated with the LVivoEF System. Average values were calculated for each variable measured by Manual Biplane Method (MBP) and Pearson correlation coefficients were calculated between MBP and L-VivolEF results. The primary end point defined for this study was met with a correlation coefficient calculated for biplane EF (r-0.88, p<OO0l).

performance_claims.endpoint: Biplane LVEF agreement vs manual biplane (MBP)
performance_claims.quote: In the blinded clinical trial, ultrasound clips of 100 subjects were evaluated with the LVivo System. Average values were calculated for each variable measured by Manual Biplane Method (MBP) and Pearson correlation coefficients were calculated between MBP and LVivoEF results. The primary end point defined for this study was met with a correlation coefficient calculated for biplane EF (r=0.88, p<0001).

performance_claims.endpoint: GLS by LVivoSG vs Siemens Velocity Vector Imaging (VVI)
performance_claims.metric: Pearson r / ICC / kappa / sensitivity / specificity
performance_claims.value: r=0.85 (p<0.0001); ICC=0.92; kappa=0.77 (Normal/Abnormal, cutoff -12% LVivoSG vs -15% VVI); specificity 0.86, sensitivity 0.95; mean difference -3%
performance_claims.comparator: Semi-automated VVI (Siemens syngo) applied by an expert echocardiologist
performance_claims.dataset_description: Retrospective, single-center study (Soroka University Medical Center, Israel); exams collected prospectively under protocol 100 rev 03; 3 apical views (4CH, 2CH, 3CH). Number of subjects in the LVivoSG analysis not stated.
performance_claims.quote: The results showed that the primary end point was successfully met with a very good correlation between LVivoSG and VVI for GLS ( r=0.85, p<0.0001). Excellent inter -observer reliability between methods for GLS, was also demonstrated by intraclass correlation ( ICC=0.92). ... The agreement by kappa coefficient was also very good ( kappa=0.77) and specificity and sensitivity were high (0.86 and 0.95 respectively) emphasizing the similari ty between methods. Average difference of -3% between VVI and LVivoSG was found.

performance_claims.endpoint: Wall-motion score index (WMSI) by LVivoSG vs visual estimation by physicians

The agreement calculated by ICC was very good (ICC=0.86). ... The accuracy indicated by AUC=0.86 was very good and the specificity and  sensitivity were 0.8 and 0.78 respectively.

performance_claims.endpoint: Coronary-territory strain (LVivoSG vs VVI) and wall motion (LVivoSG vs visual)
performance_claims.value: Strain ICC LAD 0.86, RCA 0.84, CX 0.90 (CX kappa 0.71, spec 0.80, sens 0.94); WM ICC LAD 0.80, RCA 0.82, CX 0.83; AUC LAD 0.86, RCA 0.82, CX 0.81; LAD kappa 0.65 (cutoff 0.34), CX kappa 0.51

performance_claims.quote: Good agreement was demonstrated comparing territories of coronary arteries between strain by LVivoSG and strain by VVI with ICC =0.86, 0.84 and 0.9 for LAD, RCA and CX respectively. ... The ICC comparing LAD, RCA and CX was 0.8, 0.82 and 0.83  respectively. ... The accuracy by AUC for LAD, RCA and CX was  0.86, 0.82 and 0.81  respectively.

training_data.description: No FDA summary in this family states training-set size. The Philips Lumify K232500 summary (Auto EF = LVivo EF) states the 80-patient test set 'were completely distinct from that used during training of the algorithm' but gives no training size.

validation_data.description: Per-clearance validation sets: 83 subjects (K130779); 100 subjects EF + single-center Soroka SG study (K161382); single-center Philips-system RV set of unstated size and 226 bladder images (K200232); 100 patients (K210053); 121 + 40 patients (K240553 PLAX); 101 exams from 4 sites (K243235 CE-EF); 170 exams from 3 sites plus 101-patient Taiwan set (K243862 SWM).

prior_validations.description: Philips Lumify Auto EF (K232500, 2023-10-26): 'Auto EF is a new Artificial Intelligence (AI) feature ... based on the LVivo EF algorithm developed by DiA. Lumify Auto EF Quantification feature is a subset of LVivo platform.' Clinical performance: 80 patients (29% female, age 64±14, BMI 26.4), A4CH clips on Lumify; EF r=0.82 (95% CI 0.72-0.88) vs average manual tracing; EDV r=0.95, ESV r=0.94; 76/80 clips (95%) processed; test data stated to be distinct from training data.

GE Vscan Extend LVivo EF app support page: 'This app has been developed by and licensed from DiA Imaging Analysis Ltd.'; apical 4CH only, modified Simpson's; manufacturer-stated accuracy EF ±15 percentage points (-3 point bias), EDV/ESV ±35 mL; valid ranges EF 20-80%, EDV 60-240 mL, ESV 15-140 mL; not for pediatric cardiology.

DiA press release 2018-09-18: LVivo EF available on GE Healthcare Vscan Extend handheld; described as first AI-powered automated EF app running in the low-memory environment of mobile ultrasound; no performance data in the release.
Philips press release 2021-03-02: partnership to integrate DiA's FDA-cleared/CE-marked LVivo Toolbox; Philips owns a minority interest in DiA; 'thousands of end users worldwide'.

Philips press release 2024-06-04: EPIQ CVx / Affiniti CVx AI platform includes 'FDA-cleared and CE-marked software solutions from DiA Imaging Analysis' including an automated segmental wall motion scoring tool.

papers.title: Assessment and validation of a novel fast fully automated artificial intelligence left ventricular ejection fraction quantification software
papers.key_result: LVivoEF (non-contrast A4CH, no manual correction) vs cardiac MRI in 242 of 273 consecutive patients: r=0.890 (physician EF vs cMRI r=0.891); bias 3.63±7.40 EF points (underestimation) vs 0.33±7.52 for physician EF; similar in 126 UEA and 116 unenhanced studies.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Powered Measurement of Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction Using a Handheld Ultrasound Device
papers.key_result: LVivo on a handheld device (A4CH) vs 3D LVEF on a stationary echocardiograph in 112 cardiology inpatients: r=0.92 (95% CI 0.87-0.95); mean difference -0.61% (95% CI -1.89 to 0.68); accurate when image quality at least good.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Powered Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction Analysis Using the LVivoEF Tool for COVID-19 Patients
papers.key_result: Real-time LVivoEF on a handheld device vs blinded echocardiographer in 42 COVID-19 inpatients: correlation 0.774, kappa 0.797 for LVEF<50%; sensitivity 72.7%, specificity 100%; AI-based LVEF<50% associated with composite adverse outcome (adjusted OR 6.40).

papers.title: Empowering Medical Students: Harnessing Artificial Intelligence for Precision Point-of-Care Echocardiography Assessment of Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction
papers.key_result: Medical students using a handheld device with an AI-based automatic LVEF tool (abstract does not name the tool; same group's companion paper names LVivoEF): students+AI vs cardiologists correlation 0.83 vs 0.51 for students' visual estimate; AI failed in 6/88 cases.

papers.title: Artificial Intelligence-Based Left Ventricular Ejection Fraction by Medical Students for Mortality and Readmission Prediction
papers.key_result: AI-based reduced LVEF (<50%) obtained by medical students on a handheld device (tool not named in abstract) independently predicted 1-year mortality/cardiovascular readmission (HR 2.717, 95% CI 1.083-6.817).

papers.title: Pragmatic Evaluation of a Deep-Learning Algorithm to Automate Ejection Fraction on Hand-Held, Point-of-Care Echocardiography in a Cardiac Surgical Operating Room
papers.journal: Journal of Cardiothoracic and Vascular Anesthesia
papers.key_result: Philips Lumify Auto EF (LVivo EF per K232500) vs Simpson's method in 54 A4CH clips from cardiac surgical patients: r=0.56 overall (bias -10.17%), r=0.86 in 27 adequate-quality clips, r=0.46 in inadequate clips; expert visual EF r=0.80.

papers.title: The measurement of the left ventricle ejection fraction by a bedside FoCUS examination
papers.key_result: Bedside FoCUS in 59 emergency-medicine patients: 'Lvivo app' EF 39.5±12.0% vs standard echo 53.7±11.1%; r=0.571, Bland-Altman mean -13.3% (Quinones-equation EF r=0.694, bias -2.3%); authors attribute the app's underestimation to unselected image quality.

clinical_trials.title: Automated Left Ventricular Function Evaluation by LVivoEF
clinical_trials.status: UNKNOWN (last known ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING, verified 2012-01); sponsor DiA Imaging Analysis Ltd; prospective observational, estimated enrollment 100; start 2011-11

open_questions: K161382: number of subjects in the LVivoSG (strain/wall motion) validation is not stated in the summary; only the 100-subject EF cohort is quantified.
K200232: number of patients in the LVivo RV validation is not stated (only '22 months' of retrospective collection, single center).
K210053: summary gives acceptance criteria but no numeric results for the neural-network LVivo EF update.
K240553: bias/LOA/correlation table for the 40-patient US PLAX dataset is an embedded image and not present in the extracted text.
K243235: sex breakdown is internally inconsistent in the summary (52/94 female 55% and 59/94 male 62%).

K243862: the ICC table (GT vs LVivo SWM 0.85; expert pairs 0.64/0.74/0.81) sits under the 'Second Validation Set' header in the text extraction but the prose attributes an ICC analysis to the primary set; which set it belongs to is ambiguous.
Training-set size for any LVivo module is not disclosed in any FDA summary or in the papers read; K232500 only states test data were distinct from training data.
product_url: DiA's site (dia-analysis.com, cited in press releases) did not resolve from this session's network; no Philips-hosted LVivo product page was located.
Dadon 2023 (Int J Clin Pract) and Dadon 2024 (Diagnostics) abstracts do not name LVivo; inclusion rests on the same group's LVivoEF COVID paper using the same handheld+AI setup.
Whether the 2014-2019 handheld deployments (GE Vscan Extend) correspond to K130779/K161382 or K200232 (Android option) is not stated in the summaries.

families.summary: Standalone server application that receives complete echo exams in DICOM, automatically identifies the apical 4-, 2- and 3-chamber clips, runs the cleared LVivo EF and (from v2.0) LVivo Strain modules without user interaction, and sends EF/GLS results to PACS for clinician review. The 2025 version can alternatively invoke FDA-cleared TomTec Auto EF and Auto Strain. Indications added 'Age >18' in 2021.
families.intended_use_quote: LVivo platform is intended for non-invasive processing of ultrasound images to detect, measure, and calculate relevant medical parameters of structures and function of patients with suspected disease.
families.indications_for_use_quote: LVivo platform is intended for non-invasive processing of ultrasound images to detect, measure, and calculate relevant medical parameters of structures and function of patients with suspected disease of patients and Age >18.
embedded_ai_features: Automatic view classification/selection of apical 4CH, 2CH, 3CH clips from a full exam
Automated biplane EF via LVivo EF module
Automated GLS (per view and global) via LVivo Strain module
Optional invocation of TomTec Auto EF / Auto Strain (K243331)

clearances.changes_summary: Special 510(k): new standalone server configuration that auto-selects clips and runs the cleared LVivo EF module offline; no manual adjustment/editing, no volume curve, EF module only.

LVivo Seamless v2.0: adds LVivo Strain module (segmental and global longitudinal strain, GLS per view) and 3CH view selection; adds editing of output results; indications add 'Age >18'. Reference device K210053. Summary header says Special 510(k); openFDA lists Traditional.
Special 510(k): adds the ability to run automated EF and strain analysis by another FDA-cleared third-party software (TomTec Auto EF / Auto Strain) in addition to LVivo EF/Strain.

families.company: DiA Imaging Analysis Ltd. (a Philips company since May 2023; earlier trade name DiACardio Ltd.)
deployment: on-device real-time (software component/API integrated by OEMs into ultrasound systems)
families.summary: Real-time AI image-quality scoring for the apical 4-chamber view: an algorithm plus API supplied as a software component for OEM integration that grades the left ventricle (2023) and, from 2024, the right ventricle on a 0-100% scale (0-60 poor/red, 60-80 medium/orange, 80-100 good/green) while the user scans. Validated retrospectively against sonographer quality tags and prospectively with point-of-care physicians on Lumify. Concept compared by the sponsor to Caption Guidance.
families.intended_use_quote: LVivo platform is intended for non-invasive processing of ultrasound images to detect, measure, and calculate relevant medical parameters of structures and function of patients with suspected disease. In addition, it has the ability to provide Quality Score feedback.
families.indications_for_use_quote: LVivo platform is intended for non-invasive processing of ultrasound images to detect, measure, and calculate relevant medical parameters of structures and function of patients with suspected disease. In addition, it has the ability to provide Quality Score feedback.
embedded_ai_features: AI-based real-time image quality score for LV from apical 4CH (K222970)
AI-based real-time image quality score for RV from apical 4CH (K240769)
I/O via API for OEM integration

clearances.changes_summary: Initial clearance: adds an IQS algorithm + API to the LVivo platform providing a real-time quality score for the LV from the apical 4CH view; provided as a software component for integration into OEM ultrasound devices (medical device accessory). Indications add 'the ability to provide Quality Score feedback'. (Comparison table cites predicate as 'K219953', an apparent typo for K210053.)
Special 510(k): extends IQS to the right ventricle from the apical 4CH view; same grading ranges and API; minimum spec 8 GB RAM, Windows 10+, Intel i3.

performance_claims.endpoint: LV IQS agreement with sonographer quality tagging (retrospective)
performance_claims.value: 81% (criterion 75%); 22,663 frames
performance_claims.dataset_description: 100 exams acquired with different ultrasound devices and various cardiac pathologies (per NCT05563701: drawn from 424 exams collected at two centers, each with 10 clips representing typical scanning errors)
performance_claims.quote: 100 patient examinations were used for the validation. Inclusion criteria: Age>18, patients referred to routine Echo examination . Exclusion criteria: Subjects who fail to meet any inclusion criteria . Total of 22,663 frames were analyzed. The overall agreement was agreement between the LVivo IQS and quality tagging by the experienced sonographers was 81%

performance_claims.endpoint: Prospective POC use of LV IQS by interns (Lumify)
performance_claims.metric: % exams reaching at least 'Medium' score / % clinically interpretable
performance_claims.value: 90% of patients with visual image quality 3-5 (ACEP) reached at least Medium (criterion 80%); 93% of those clips clinically interpretable (criterion 90%)
performance_claims.comparator: Visual ACEP quality score; expert echocardiologist interpretability review
performance_claims.dataset_description: 64 patients with POCUS indication scanned by POC interns; ACEP image quality 1-2 excluded
performance_claims.quote: a. In 90% of the patients with image quality 3-5 by visual estimation it was possible to obtain at least "Medium" quality score by LVivo IQS b. 93% of the above saved clips were clinically interpretable

performance_claims.endpoint: RV IQS agreement with sonographer quality tagging (retrospective)
performance_claims.value: 77% (criterion 75%); 49,623 frames
performance_claims.quote: 100 patient examinations were used for the validation. ... A total of 49,623 frames were analyzed. The overall agreement was agreement between the LVivo IQS  (RV) and quality tagging by the experienced sonographers was 77%

performance_claims.endpoint: Prospective POC use of RV IQS by intern physicians
performance_claims.metric: % exams reaching at least 'Medium' / % clinically interpretable
performance_claims.value: 85% of ACEP 3-5 exams reached at least Medium (criterion 80%); 92% clinically interpretable by majority of three expert cardiologists (criterion 90%)
performance_claims.comparator: ACEP score; majority of three echo cardiologists
performance_claims.dataset_description: 182 patients with POCUS indication, scanned in point-of-care settings by physicians in internship
performance_claims.quote: a. In 85% of the patients with image quality 3-5 by visual estimation it was possible to obtain at least "Medium" quality score by LVivo IQS b. 92% of the above saved clips were clinically interpretable

training_data.description: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05563701 (sponsor DiA): 424 examinations (10 clips each) collected at two medical centers with sonographer quality tags were 'randomly split into training and clinical validation sets' with the validation set fixed at 100 examinations; the training-set count is not stated explicitly (arithmetically at most 324 exams). FDA summaries do not mention training data.

validation_data.description: Retrospective: 100 exams (22,663 frames LV; 49,623 frames RV). Prospective: 64 patients (LV, K222970) and 182 patients (RV, K240769) scanned on Lumify by POC physicians at two centers per NCT05563701.
validation_data.source: K222970/K240769 summaries; NCT05563701 states random train/validation split

prior_validations.description: DiA press release 2023-02-06 on LVivo IQS clearance: 91% of images saved by point-of-care residents were clinically interpretable per cardiologists; PI Dr. Lior Fuchs, Soroka Medical Center; described as first of DiA's 9 FDA-cleared solutions to give real-time feedback.

clinical_trials.title: Evaluation of the LVivo Image Quality Scoring (IQS)
clinical_trials.status: COMPLETED; observational prospective; actual enrollment 164; sponsor DiA Imaging Analysis Ltd; Part 1 retrospective 100-exam validation vs sonographer tagging, Part 2 live POC scans on Lumify at two centers

open_questions: No peer-reviewed publication of the LVivo IQS validation was found on PubMed (queries: 'LVivo IQS', 'LVivo', real-time quality score terms).
Ultrasound device mix for the 100-exam retrospective sets is described only as 'different ultrasound devices'.
Exact training-set size is not stated; NCT05563701 gives only the total (424) and validation (100) counts.
Number of sites for the K240769 prospective RV study is not stated in the summary.
Press release states 91% interpretability vs 93% in the K222970 summary; discrepancy unexplained.

notes: All 12 K-numbers read in full from the extracted FDA summary text. Decision dates/product codes taken from openFDA. K130779 text is OCR of a scanned 2013 letter (values transcribed as printed, e.g. 'r-0.88, p<OO0l'). K212466 is labeled Special 510(k) in the summary but Traditional in openFDA; openFDA retained. Lumify Auto EF (Philips K232500) was confirmed to be 'a subset of LVivo platform' and is cited as a prior validation, not as a clearance of this family. Papers included only where the abstract names LVivo/LVivoEF or (MacKay 2024) uses Lumify Auto EF; two Dadon papers are included with a caveat that their abstracts do not name the tool. Sveric 2024 (Int J Cardiol) and Kane 2026 (EHJ Digital Health) were reviewed and excluded (no LVivo attribution / different vendor). Company site dia-analysis.com was unreachable from this session; URL recorded as stated in DiA press releases.
